title: Read a date a user typed

blocks.text: A form lets users type a date in any of three forms:
Write `UserDates.parse(String text)`. It returns the date in an `Optional`, or an empty `Optional` when the text is not a date in one of these forms. It never throws.

items: A day the month does not have is **refused**: `2024-02-30` is not a date, and must not become February 29.
A `null` text gives an empty result.
The month abbreviations are US English (`Jan`, `Feb`, `Mar`, ... `Sep`, ...) **whatever the server's default locale** is.

cases.says: Each of the three accepted forms gives its date, and any other text gives an empty result.
February 30 and April 31 are refused rather than moved to the month's last day.
A null input gives an empty result instead of an exception.
15-Mar-2024 is read on a server whose default locale is German.

concepts: A formatter that prints or reads month or day names needs an explicit Locale, or the server's default locale decides the words.
Parsing throws DateTimeParseException for bad text and NullPointerException for null, so user input is parsed through a method that tries each accepted format and returns an Optional.
A formatter from ofPattern resolves SMART, silently moving 2024-02-30 to February 29, while ResolverStyle.STRICT refuses it.
